reasons: Both deliver the same correct NULL-safe NOT EXISTS query with a relative 90-day cutoff, so the rubric is fully met by each and the decision rests on the surrounding notes. A adds the boundary-semantics note (>= includes exactly 90 days ago, flip to > for the other reading) and points at pg_indexes, the view that actually shows index definitions, while B points at pg_stat_user_indexes, which reports usage rather than the indexed columns it tells the user to check. B's refusal to guess at the plan is honest but A gives the same caveat plus the concrete EXPLAIN check and what a good plan looks like.

A: Claims the planner treats NOT IN and NOT EXISTS as an anti-join 'either way'; PostgreSQL generally cannot convert a NOT IN subquery to an anti-join because of NULL semantics and uses a hashed SubPlan instead.
B: Suggests checking pg_stat_user_indexes to see whether an existing index covers the (customer_id, created_at) prefix; that view exposes index names and usage counters, not the indexed columns, so it cannot answer that question (pg_indexes or \d orders can).
